questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Egypt?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Egypt article.

questions.proof: Cairo is the capital, largest city, and most important cultural center, while Alexandria is the second-largest city and an important hub of industry and tourism.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Egypt?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Egypt on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Egypt article.

questions.proof: It is also bordered by the Red Sea to the east, Sudan to the south, and Libya to the west.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Egypt?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Languages” part of the Egypt article.

questions.proof: The official language in Egypt is Arabic.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In the northeast, the Gulf of Aqaba separates Egypt from _____ and Saudi Arabia.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Egypt”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Egypt article.

questions.proof: In the northeast, the Gulf of Aqaba separates Egypt from Jordan and Saudi Arabia.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “To the northeast is the region of the Southern Levant comprising _____ and the Gaza Strip, which is part of Palestine.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “comprising”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Egypt article.

questions.proof: To the northeast is the region of the Southern Levant comprising Israel and the Gaza Strip, which is part of Palestine.
